notes.front: What does GEMMA stand for?
notes.back: GEMeentelijke Model Architectuur (Municipal Model Architecture): the national reference architecture for all Dutch municipalities.

notes.front: Which organisation publishes and maintains GEMMA?
notes.back: The Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten (VNG, Association of Netherlands Municipalities); published on GEMMA Online.

notes.front: On which national reference architecture does GEMMA build?
notes.back: The Nederlandse Overheid Referentie Architectuur (NORA, Dutch Government Reference Architecture).

notes.front: Order these reference architectures from broadest to most specific: NORA, EIRA, GEMMA.
notes.back: European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA, European governments) → Nederlandse Overheid Referentie Architectuur (NORA, Dutch government) → GEMeentelijke Model Architectuur (GEMMA, Dutch municipalities).

notes.front: What is the main purpose of the GEMeentelijke Model Architectuur (GEMMA)?
notes.back: Help municipalities steer ICT developments in coherence: developing, building, buying and implementing under architecture so solutions work together, and giving management an overview.

notes.front: How does the GEMMA glossary define a referentiearchitectuur (reference architecture)?
notes.back: A template solution (sjabloonoplossing) for the architecture of a particular domain.

notes.front: Which modelling language does the GEMeentelijke Model Architectuur (GEMMA) use?
notes.back: ArchiMate. Elements are ordered by function and/or architecture layer to show coherence of processes, information provision and technical architecture.

notes.front: Why must a municipality translate the GEMMA models rather than adopt them verbatim?
notes.back: Municipalities differ in organisational set-up and vision, so the reference models must be translated to the own municipal context.

notes.front: What are the four layers of the GEMMA Basisarchitectuur?
notes.back:
1. Strategie en motivatie (strategy & motivation)
2. Bedrijfsarchitectuur (business architecture)
3. Informatiearchitectuur (information architecture)
4. Technische architectuur (technical architecture)

notes.front: What does the bedrijfsarchitectuur (business architecture) describe?
notes.back: What the municipality does, which organisational units do it, and how (business processes). It forms the basis for the information architecture.

notes.front: For which GEMMA layers are hierarchical overzichtsdiagrammen (overview diagrams) used?
notes.back: Strategie en motivatie, Bedrijfsarchitectuur and Technische architectuur. They group elements hierarchically by a criterion.

notes.front: What is the procesarchitectuur (process architecture) in GEMMA?
notes.back: Part of the business architecture containing principles and agreements for setting up business processes.

notes.front: In the GEMMA procesarchitectuur, what is the role ketenpartner (chain partner)?
notes.back: A role for processes handled partly outside the municipality, e.g. the company producing passports or a body doing Wet maatschappelijke ondersteuning (WMO, Social Support Act) assessments. They are roles, not organisations.

notes.front: What are architectuurprincipes (architecture principles) according to GEMMA?
notes.back: Directive statements that ensure a coherent set-up of the organisation. They translate goals, needs and policy starting points and bridge to execution.

notes.front: How does the GEMMA ArchiMate model define a principe?
notes.back: A qualitative statement of intent that the architecture must meet.

notes.front: Are the GEMMA architecture principles mandatory rules?
notes.back: No. They express best practices / objectives; a municipality decides itself how to apply them. Support (draagvlak) among the target group is essential.

notes.front: Who is the target group of the GEMMA architecture principles?
notes.back: Everyone involved in changes to municipal processes and information provision.

notes.front: How did the (pre-2025) GEMMA principles relate to the NORA principles?
notes.back: All Nederlandse Overheid Referentie Architectuur (NORA) principles were adopted in GEMMA, supplemented by three GEMMA-specific principles.

notes.front: What was the outcome of the 2024/2025 renewal of the GEMMA architecture principles?
notes.back: One set of GEMMA principles in line with the Common Ground vision. The separate Common Ground information-architecture and realisation principles became obsolete.

notes.front: Name four GEMMA Gegevenslandschap (data landscape) principles with many links to the general GEMMA principles.
notes.back:
• We werken met componenten
• We zorgen dat informatiebeveiliging en privacy op orde zijn
• We leggen gegevens eenmalig vast en vragen op bij de bron
• We standaardiseren maximaal

notes.front: Which two Gegevenslandschap principles relate most strongly to putting citizens' interests first?
notes.back:
• We zijn transparant waar mogelijk
• We faciliteren regie op gegevens (control over one's own data)

notes.front: Describe the layered model of principles (GEMMA → Gegevenslandschap → Common Ground).
notes.back: Principles in a higher layer frame those below. Example: Gegevenslandschap principle 'We werken met componenten' was concretised by the former Common Ground realisation principle 'We ontwikkelen en gebruiken NLX als gateway'.

notes.front: How does GEMMA define a bedrijfsfunctie (business function)?
notes.back: Activities grouped together because they require comparable resources, knowledge or competences.

notes.front: What is a referentiecomponent (reference component)?
notes.back: A building block of municipal information provision: a modular, independently deployable and replaceable part of a software system that groups logically related functionality and offers it via well-defined interfaces.

notes.front: What is the modelled chain between reference components and business functions?
notes.back: Referentiecomponent → realises → applicatieservice → used by → bedrijfsfunctie.

notes.front: In the per-domain views 'business function model with reference components', what is left out and why?
notes.back: The intermediate applicatieservices (application services), for readability.

notes.front: Give an example of domain-specific vs. generic municipal software per GEMMA.
notes.back:
Specific: a vergunningensysteem (permit system).
Generic: a zaaksysteem (case management system) or a service bus.

notes.front: How did the scope of the GEMMA applicatieservice-model change over time?
notes.back: From only e-dienstverlening (electronic service delivery) to supporting all municipal business processes, with a clearer split between generic and domain-specific functionality.

notes.front: Is the applicatieservice-model normative?
notes.back: It is a reference architecture and therefore directive (richtinggevend) for arranging municipal information management.

notes.front: What does each GEMMA domeinarchitectuur (domain architecture) work out?
notes.back: A bedrijfsfunctiemodel (business function model) and an applicatieservice-model for that domain, e.g. the Sociaal domein.

notes.front: What does the view 'Referentiecomponenten en bedrijfsfuncties' show?
notes.back: In a simpler hierarchical set-up, which business functions are supported by which reference components.

notes.front: In the overview diagrams, what does the bottom block Buitengemeentelijk contain?
notes.back: Elements outside the municipality that are relevant to it: VNG, sectoral partners and national government.

notes.front: Which tool maps supplier software onto GEMMA reference components and standards?
notes.back: The GEMMA Softwarecatalogus.

notes.front: What is GIBIT and how does it use GEMMA?
notes.back: Gemeentelijke Inkoop bij IT (GIBIT, Municipal IT Procurement) toolbox; GEMMA is the frame for its ICT quality norms.

notes.front: What is the relationship between GEMMA and Common Ground?
notes.back: Common Ground is the informatiekundige visie (information vision) of municipalities; GEMMA works out the generic functions needed to realise it (and since 2025 carries its principles).

notes.front: Core idea of Common Ground regarding data?
notes.back: Decouple data from work processes and applications; query data at the source instead of copying and storing it repeatedly.

notes.front: Name the five layers of the renewed Common Ground vijflaagsmodel (top → bottom).
notes.back:
1. Interactie
2. Procesinrichting
3. Connectiviteit
4. Diensten
5. Gegevensbronnen

notes.front: Name the five layers of the original Common Ground five-layer model.
notes.back: Interactie, Proces, Integratie, Services, Data.

notes.front: Which kinds of generic functions sit in the top two layers of the Common Ground model?
notes.back: Interactie and Procesinrichting: interaction with citizens, businesses and staff, and executing municipal processes.

notes.front: What does the middle layer Connectiviteit do?
notes.back: Facilitates communication between functions in the upper and lower layers.

notes.front: What do the bottom two layers (Diensten, Gegevensbronnen) provide?
notes.back: Responsible, standardised storage of data and its disclosure (ontsluiting).

notes.front: Why does the five-layer model group functions per layer?
notes.back: To separate process-execution functionality from recording/providing data in source registrations; putting bounded functionality in separate components yields a more modular information provision.

notes.front: What is expected of a dienstenafnemer (service consumer) in the Common Ground model?
notes.back: Slim user interfaces that maximally use data from source registrations.

notes.front: What is expected of a dienstenaanbieder (service provider) in the Common Ground model?
notes.back: Standardised Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) that consumers use to access source data.

notes.front: Can one party or application cover multiple roles/functions in the Common Ground model?
notes.back: Yes: parties can fulfil one or more roles and applications can realise one or more functions.

notes.front: What is GEMMA Verwerkingenlogging?
notes.back: A GEMMA standard: information model + API specifications for logging processing of personal data, so municipalities can meet the accountability duty of the Algemene Verordening Gegevensbescherming (AVG, Dutch name for the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)).

notes.front: What is GEMMA Verwerkingsactiviteiten?
notes.back: Standardised information model + APIs for the verwerkingsregister (register of processing activities) required by the Algemene Verordening Gegevensbescherming (AVG), holding metadata such as legal basis, purpose and categories of personal data.

notes.front: What is Zaakgericht Werken (ZGW) in the GEMMA context?
notes.back: Zaakgericht Werken (ZGW, case-oriented working): a GEMMA theme with a set of VNG API standards (ZGW APIs) for case handling.

notes.front: What does the Katern GEMMA Verbinden cover?
notes.back: It translates principles and guidelines into concrete designs of the information architecture, incl. patterns for offering open data and connecting the municipality with its customers.

notes.front: GEMMA 2 (2015): name two cross-cutting positions it took.
notes.back: 'Verbinden' (connecting) is not a thing but is everywhere; security and privacy are an important concern everywhere. It also distinguishes generic vs. domain-specific functions and reuses the Generieke Digitale Infrastructuur (GDI, Generic Digital Infrastructure).

notes.front: GEMMA definition: informatievoorziening (information provision)
notes.back: The whole of people, resources and measures aimed at the information needs of the organisation.

notes.front: GEMMA definition: informatie vs. gegeven
notes.back:
Informatie: the meaning people give to data in a context.
Gegeven: a recorded observation or assertion about a property of an object.

notes.front: GEMMA definition: standaard
notes.back: A document with recognised agreements, specifications or criteria about a product, service or method.
